result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A plots nominal rent next to an index-scaled counterfactual line on a zero-based axis, which makes the gap visible. Its title still leads with the dramatic 48%, the ~12% real figure is never stated, and the series use a detached legend, though the end values are labeled. B shows only the nominal bars, and the index appears just as text, so the adjustment can't be seen in the chart; its axis also has no dollar units. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B plots nominal rent next to a price-index counterfactual line ($1,564), uses a zero baseline and dollar labels, and explains that rent outpaced prices. It doesn't state the ~12% real increase, its legend is detached (though end values are labeled at the lines), and the title leads with the dramatic 48%. A shows only nominal bars headlined '+48%', mentions the index only in text, and its title is a plain label rather than a finding.
